scope: Six bounded case files: Delhi Safe City official metric reconciliation; Mumbai CCTV/Safe City asset join; CISF land payment; CAPF professional-tax audit; CRPF named supplier award; Pahalgam legal-stage chronology. No claim of exhaustive national coverage, personal guilt scoring or calibrated prediction.

cases.title: Delhi Safe City: reconcile conflicting integration counts
cases.question: Are the February and July 2026 integration figures measuring the same accepted camera population?
cases.finding: Two official statements give materially different existing-camera integration counts. This is a reporting and acceptance question, not a computed loss.

geography.label: Delhi
geography.basis: Administrative/project association; no operational deployment or exact assets mapped

claims.text: PIB on 16 February 2026 says more than 15,000 existing cameras were integrated; an MHA reply on 5 August reports 5,852 of 15,000 as of 30 July.
claims.response: The July reply reports 7,974 new cameras installed across fixed/PTZ and ANPR categories and a partly operational ICCC; it does not report zero delivery.
claims.alternative: Staged interfaces, live accepted feeds versus configured connections, reporting lags or category/transcription errors could explain different counts.
claims.falsifier: Obtain dated asset crosswalks and acceptance criteria. Show that 5,852 is a subset or a different stage of more than 15,000, or obtain a correction.

whatWeKnow: Both counts were cross-read in official documents.
New-camera installations and integration of existing cameras are different metrics.
whatWeDoNotKnow: No ₹857 crore paid total, missing-camera monetary amount or beneficiary transfer is inferred.

nextRecords.holder: Delhi Police Safe City project office / C-DAC / MHA
nextRecords.purpose: Compare populations, dates and acceptance stages
Test whether payments required technical acceptance

limits: No camera-level operational data is published here.
A programme headline cost is not a corruption loss.

cases.title: Mumbai: CCTV award, Safe City delivery and unjoined assets
cases.question: Which paid assets are covered by GVPR Phase III versus separately reported Safe City targets?
cases.finding: A ₹2,098.92 crore supplier appointment is documented. July 2026 Safe City reports delivered cameras and other completed components, with some components still in progress. The asset and funding crosswalk is missing; repeated spending cannot be inferred.

geography.label: Mumbai
geography.basis: City procurement/programme association; no cameras or residences geolocated

claims.text: The Phase III acceptance and Safe City status records do not establish whether cameras or maintenance were funded twice.
claims.response: Official reply reports 5,422 cameras achieved and central share fully released. The government resolution describes QCBS, four participants, two technically qualified bidders and a negotiated price.
claims.alternative: Ordinary replacement, maintenance of different assets, deliberate de-scoping and separate funding streams can explain multiple programmes. Matching city or camera counts is not matching assets.
claims.falsifier: Reconcile itemised bills of quantities, asset IDs, old-contract closure and Phase III de-scoping against the Safe City ledger. Disjoint assets or credited overlap would weaken the duplicate-payment hypothesis.
missingRecords: Phase II and III bills of quantities

whatWeKnow: GVPR accepted amount includes GST; administrative sanction includes contingency.
Maharashtra ASUMP central allocations are not Mumbai Safe City spending.
Full central release coexists with some components still in progress.
whatWeDoNotKnow: Actual supplier payment, subcontractors and ultimate beneficiaries remain unverified.

cases.title: CISF land: paid price, disputed possession and separate sanction
cases.question: Why was land paid for without verified encumbrance clearance, and was ₹6.53 crore later adjusted?
cases.finding: CAG records ₹6.53 crore paid to MoHUA in March 2016 and funds blocked for over nine years. It also includes CISF’s response and proposed alternate-land adjustment. The ₹261.24 crore construction approval is separate.

geography.label: Delhi
geography.basis: Administrative/project association; no operational deployment or exact assets mapped

geography.label: Faridabad
geography.basis: Proposed alternate-land association, not an exact site

claims.text: CAG found no Board assessment record, non-encumbrance certificate or completed measurement/boundary record despite the 2016 payment.
claims.response: CISF said MoHUA concealed litigation. CAG acknowledged possible non-disclosure but held that CISF due-diligence requirements still applied.
claims.alternative: Interdepartmental non-disclosure, legacy title litigation and administrative delay can explain the failure without a private kickback. A missing file does not prove an assessment never occurred.
claims.falsifier: Produce contemporaneous Board assessment, non-encumbrance certificate, court-case check or certified alternate-land adjustment/refund and possession records.

whatWeKnow: Payment recipient is MoHUA, not an identified private company.
The ₹261.24 crore sanction is not proved paid.
An alternate-land process was reported in May 2025, with the earlier amount to be adjusted.
The audit records a formal November 2016 handover on an as-is basis. That paperwork is distinct from unobstructed, usable possession, which the audit found unachieved.
whatWeDoNotKnow: Whether adjustment, refund or usable possession occurred after May 2025.
Whether any official intentionally misrepresented title.

nextRecords.purpose: Test remediation and allocation of responsibility

limits: Audit finding is not a criminal judgment; no embezzlement or private beneficiary is claimed.
The 1992 land litigation is dated context outside the 15-year review window.

actors.authority: Land acquisition buyer subject to MHA assessment guidelines
actors.incentive: Analytical possibility: obtain required facilities promptly while controlling title risk; not a finding of private intent.
Analytical possibility: reallocate public land while managing legacy claims; not a finding of private intent.

informationThen: The 1992 litigation preceded payment, but CISF says it was not disclosed; we cannot assume CISF knew.

options.label: Verify Board assessment and encumbrances before payment
options.expectedObservableOutcome: Documented title and possession check, or delay pending clearance.

options.label: Accept as-is allotment and seek remediation later

claims.text: CAG §2.11 reports ₹26.40 crore not deducted over selected periods. Unit replies invoked pending exemptions, lack of notices or armed-force classification.
claims.response: CAG says no applicable exemption was identified in these six states; Maharashtra and Karnataka exemptions were counterexamples. MHA reply was awaited in October 2025.
claims.alternative: Legal classification disputes, payroll configuration errors and pending exemption requests are ordinary alternatives. Errors in period/rate or valid retrospective exemptions could change liability.
claims.falsifier: Recompute unit-period payroll using the law and exemptions applicable then. Tax challans, recoveries and valid exemption notifications could reduce or remove outstanding liability.

whatWeKnow: Tax non-deduction is not a transfer to a contractor.

cases.title: Pahalgam: attribution, charges and evidentiary boundaries
cases.question: What do inspected public records establish about attribution and funding, and what remains unproven?
cases.finding: NIA filings allege LeT/TRF planning; the July 2026 supplement names Hafiz Saeed. A reported court order distinguishes harbouring from execution. Cash origin and any government-funded plot are not established. No false-flag edge is admitted.

geography.label: Pahalgam
geography.basis: Historical incident association, not current operational routing

claims.text: NIA alleges LeT/TRF planned and facilitated the attack. Its official register confirms the 6 July 2026 supplementary-filing announcement naming Hafiz Saeed.
claims.response: Pakistan denied involvement in April 2025; no individual merits response or final judgment was obtained.
claims.alternative: Agency attribution may ultimately be proved, narrowed or disproved. Group nationality, location or company benefit does not identify a state funding transfer. Reporting may collapse organisational and state actors.
claims.falsifier: Inspect certified chargesheets, test forensic chain of custody against defence expert challenges, and obtain later merits orders. Correct or withdraw unsupported assertions.

claims.text: Daily Excelsior’s report of the 4 May 2026 order distinguishes alleged harbouring/omission by two local defendants from conspiracy in the actual execution.
claims.response: Earlier defence challenged insufficient evidence and delay; custody extension did not decide guilt.
claims.alternative: Legal-stage or reporting error could change this nuance. Prima facie charges cannot be converted into a conviction.
claims.falsifier: Read the certified 4 May order and subsequent orders; correct the reported role distinction if certified text differs.

claims.text: A reporter attributes to the prosecution a ₹3,000 cash payment by one attacker to Parvaiz Ahmad; no origin-of-funds ledger or independent receipt was obtained.
claims.response: No case-specific merits response or independently verified cash record was available. The reported court order limited the local defendants’ roles.
claims.alternative: Cash could be unproven, misreported, coerced or payment for food rather than proof of knowing attack financing. The upstream funder is unknown.
claims.falsifier: Obtain admissible testimony and cross-examination, any cash/receipt evidence, and the certified court assessment. Without a source chain, no join to LeT or a state budget is justified.

whatWeKnow: The 22 April 2025 attack and 26 deaths were reported. Initial filing: 15 December 2025; charge framing reportedly 4 May 2026; supplementary filing: 6 July 2026.
Multiple reports repeat the NIA; URL count is not independent evidence count.
whatWeDoNotKnow: Final trial result as of the review was not obtained.
No verified financing route from taxes, tenders, ministries or companies to this attack.
No evidentiary basis found for a false-flag conclusion.

nextRecords.record: Certified 4 May order and original/supplementary chargesheets
nextRecords.holder: NIA Special Court, Jammu / NIA public records
nextRecords.purpose: Verify roles, legal stage and admissible evidence

nextRecords.record: Public post-July 2026 docket and defence responses

limits: No operational vulnerabilities, real-time positions, route plans or private residential details included.
Benefit, motive and security failure alone do not prove a staged attack.
Reuters fetch was partial; primary NIA access was limited to register metadata.
